region: Pakistan — Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar

entries.description: Aedes aegypti dengue transmission rises after the monsoon, as standing water enables breeding; reported cases peak in the post-monsoon months (~Aug–Nov) and decline through winter. Strongest in Punjab and Sindh urban centres (Lahore, Rawalpindi, Islamabad, Karachi).

citation.organization: WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean (EMRO) — Pakistan
citation.basis: WHO EMRO Pakistan dengue situation updates and provincial surveillance consistently document a post-monsoon (Aug–Nov) seasonal peak in dengue transmission.

additional_citations.organization: Government of Punjab, Directorate General Health Services
additional_citations.basis: Provincial dengue surveillance reporting for Punjab.

entries.description: Punjab's smog season runs roughly October–January, when cooler temperatures, low wind, temperature inversions and seasonal crop-residue burning trap particulates — elevating PM2.5/PM10 and associated respiratory risk, most severely in Lahore.

citation.organization: Government of Punjab (Environmental Protection Department) — smog-season advisories; documented air-quality literature
citation.basis: Government of Punjab smog advisories and published air-quality studies document a recurring Oct–Jan smog season over Punjab, centred on Lahore. URL omitted rather than cite a non-canonical link; attribution is to the responsible authority and documented seasonality.

entries.description: In Pakistan's northern subtropical/temperate climate, seasonal influenza activity rises in the colder months and peaks in winter (~Dec–Feb).

citation.basis: WHO influenza-seasonality guidance describes winter-peaking influenza activity in northern-hemisphere temperate/subtropical zones, which includes northern Pakistan.

entries.description: 2011 saw a major dengue epidemic in Punjab, centred on Lahore — one of the largest recorded dengue outbreaks in Pakistan. Recorded qualitatively (no case counts asserted here).

citation.organization: WHO EMRO Pakistan / Government of Punjab dengue response
citation.basis: The 2011 Lahore/Punjab dengue epidemic is widely documented by WHO EMRO and the Government of Punjab as a major outbreak year.

entries.description: 2019 saw a marked nationwide dengue surge across Pakistan, with notable activity around Islamabad/Rawalpindi and other cities. Recorded qualitatively.

citation.basis: WHO EMRO Pakistan reporting documents an elevated 2019 dengue season nationally.
